es.summary: Se instaló un servicio de Windows (evento 7045) cuyo ImagePath encadena comandos con '&&' y usa rundll32 shell32.dll,ShellExec_RunDLL para lanzar PowerShell ofuscado. Es el patrón típico del launcher RUNDLL de Invoke-Obfuscation.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 7045 del Service Control Manager en el log System cuyo ImagePath contiene '&&', 'rundll32', 'shell32.dll' y 'shellexec_rundll', además de 'value', 'invoke', 'comspec' o 'iex'. Esto indica un servicio que guarda un script en una variable de entorno y lo ejecuta mediante rundll32.
es.why_it_matters: Crear servicios es una forma común de ejecutar código como SYSTEM, ya sea para moverse lateralmente o para persistir. La ofuscación (T1027) busca evadir controles y PowerShell (T1059.001) ejecuta el payload. Los instaladores legítimos casi nunca generan este patrón.
triage_steps: Revise el ImagePath completo: identifique la variable de entorno definida con 'set', el contenido asignado y el comando de PowerShell que la evalúa (IEX, Invoke-Expression, $env:, .Value).
Anote ServiceName, AccountName y StartType. Los nombres aleatorios y los servicios bajo LocalSystem con inicio a demanda son sospechosos.
Busque en el log Security del mismo host, en una ventana de +/- 15 minutos, inicios de sesión de tipo 3 y eventos 4697 para identificar la cuenta y la IP de origen.
En la telemetría de procesos, revise los hijos de services.exe: cmd.exe, rundll32.exe y powershell.exe, con sus líneas de comando y sus conexiones de red.
Revise el log de PowerShell (4103/4104) para recuperar el script ya desofuscado y extraer IOCs como URLs, IPs o hashes.
Busque el mismo ServiceName o un ImagePath parecido en otros hosts y revise alertas anteriores para la cuenta y la IP de origen.
false_positives: La regla no documenta falsos positivos conocidos.
Ejercicios de red team o pruebas de emulación autorizadas que usen Invoke-Obfuscation. Confírmelos con el equipo responsable antes de cerrar la alerta.
Herramientas de administración remota antiguas que usen rundll32 con ShellExec_RunDLL. Es poco común que además encadenen comandos con '&&'.
response_steps: Valide con el dueño del sistema si el servicio está autorizado y conserve el evento, el ImagePath y los logs de PowerShell.
Si no está autorizado, aísle el endpoint y deshabilite la cuenta que creó el servicio o restablezca su contraseña.
Una vez documentado, detenga y elimine el servicio (sc stop / sc delete) y busque más mecanismos de persistencia.
Bloquee los IOCs extraídos y busque si aparecen en el resto del entorno.
Recupere el host desde una imagen confiable si confirma la ejecución del payload y vigile que no reaparezca.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel alto se justifica porque un servicio que ejecuta PowerShell ofuscado mediante rundll32 casi siempre es malicioso y suele ejecutarse con privilegios de SYSTEM.

en.summary: A Windows service was installed (event 7045) whose ImagePath chains commands with '&&' and uses rundll32 shell32.dll,ShellExec_RunDLL to launch obfuscated PowerShell. This is the typical pattern of the Invoke-Obfuscation RUNDLL launcher.
en.what_it_detects: Service Control Manager event 7045 in the System log where ImagePath contains '&&', 'rundll32', 'shell32.dll' and 'shellexec_rundll', plus one of 'value', 'invoke', 'comspec' or 'iex'. This points to a service that stores a script in an environment variable and runs it through rundll32.
en.why_it_matters: Creating services is a common way to run code as SYSTEM, either to move laterally or to persist. Obfuscation (T1027) is used to evade defenses and PowerShell (T1059.001) runs the payload. Legitimate installers almost never produce this pattern.
triage_steps: Read the full ImagePath: find the environment variable set with 'set', what is assigned to it, and the PowerShell command that evaluates it (IEX, Invoke-Expression, $env:, .Value).
Record ServiceName, AccountName and StartType. Random names and on-demand LocalSystem services are suspicious.
In the same host's Security log, within +/- 15 minutes, look for logon type 3 and event 4697 to identify the account and source IP.
In process telemetry, check the children of services.exe: cmd.exe, rundll32.exe and powershell.exe, with their command lines and network connections.
Check PowerShell logs (4103/4104) to recover the deobfuscated script and extract IOCs such as URLs, IPs or hashes.
Search other hosts for the same ServiceName or a similar ImagePath, and review earlier alerts for the account and source IP.
false_positives: The rule lists no known false positives.
Authorized red team or emulation exercises that use Invoke-Obfuscation. Confirm with the responsible team before closing the alert.
Old remote administration tools that use rundll32 with ShellExec_RunDLL. It is rare for them to also chain commands with '&&'.
response_steps: Confirm with the system owner whether the service is authorized, and preserve the event, the ImagePath and the PowerShell logs.
If it is not authorized, isolate the endpoint and disable the account that created the service or reset its password.
Once documented, stop and delete the service (sc stop / sc delete) and hunt for other persistence mechanisms.
Block the extracted IOCs and search for them across the environment.
Rebuild the host from a trusted image if the payload is confirmed to have run, and watch for the service coming back.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because a service that runs obfuscated PowerShell through rundll32 is almost always malicious and usually runs with SYSTEM privileges.

positive.description: Service installed with the Invoke-Obfuscation RUNDLL launcher: sets an environment variable and runs it with IEX through ShellExec_RunDLL

event.ImagePath: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c "set nnr=Write-Output placeholder&&rundll32.exe shell32.dll,ShellExec_RunDLL powershell.exe -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -c IEX $env:nnr"

positive.description: Variant that uses %COMSPEC% and reads the variable with .Value, in mixed case

event.ImagePath: %COMSPEC% /c "set abc=Write-Output placeholder&&RUNDLL32 SHELL32.DLL,ShellExec_RunDll powershell -NoP (Get-Item env:abc).Value | Invoke-Expression"

negative.description: Legitimate-looking vendor service that uses rundll32 ShellExec_RunDLL without chaining commands with '&&' or using PowerShell keywords
Service that chains commands and uses IEX but does not use rundll32 or shell32.dll
